target_customer: Recreational and industrial boat builders (OEMs) who would buy modular hydrofoil systems; earlier as Boundary Layer, freight shippers and ferry operators
problem: Conventional hulls burn a lot of energy at speed. Foil systems promise fast, quiet, low energy vessels but are hard for boatbuilders to design and integrate themselves.
business_model: Hardware: sale of integrated hydrofoil systems to boatbuilders, plus direct sale of its own foiling craft (Valo Hyperfoil reservations)

founders.name: Ed Kearney
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch give no background; the YC launch page says the team has experience with America's Cup yachts, hyperloops, self-landing rockets and navy ships

founders.name: Jeremy Osborne
previous_startups: Electric Air (heat pump company, co-founder and CEO per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a renewable energy engineer with a decade in heat pump systems; Boundary Layer Technologies is described as his YC W19 company

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a foil system and a foiling vessel prototype in ten weeks on YC money was feasible, but stable foil control, hull integration and electric or hydrogen propulsion are hard for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Foil design know-how and patents could matter, but no source shows exclusive IP or customer lock-in at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the company by 2024; it partnered with Blue Orca Marine in February 2024.

market_need_then: The company claimed freight shippers wanted faster, cleaner alternatives to air freight and that ferry operators would pre-order electric vessels ($90 million in pre-orders claimed by the CEO in 2022); these are company claims.

identity.voice_and_tone: Speed and clean tech framing (fast, clean, quiet)

rebrands.why: TechCrunch reported a pivot from freight to foiling personal watercraft under the name Valo; the date of the legal rename is not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the Hyperfoil and a $1,000 refundable reservation queue; no fan community evidence found

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade and tech press, but the brand changed from Boundary Layer to Valo and name is shared with unrelated firms such as Valo Ventures.

pivots.from: Hydrofoil container ships for freight (Boundary Layer Technologies)
pivots.why: CEO described a shift from big first to fast first, per TechCrunch search snippet

pivots.to: Modular hydrofoil systems for boatbuilders (Blue Orca Marine partnership)
pivots.why: Partnership announced 2024-02-28 to supply foil systems to OEMs

outcome_analysis: Valo, formerly Boundary Layer Technologies, built a ten week hydrofoil prototype after YC, raised a reported 4.8 million dollars by mid 2022, pivoted from freight vessels to a foiling personal watercraft and then to supplying foil systems to boatbuilders, with a Blue Orca Marine partnership in February 2024. It is still active with a small team; no shutdown or layoff reports were found, and its outcome remains unresolved.
